01 / Workflow

Parallel development, isolated QA

Independent feature lanes

Multiple features develop concurrently, each with its own worktree, plan, gates and run state. Each receives separate evidence, a verdict and a PR.

Shared QA capacity

Feature commits enter one queue. Two reusable slots run Codex QA on the current VPS. This limit applies to QA, not development.

Many development lanes → shared queue → two QA slots. Startup is serialized; ready environments validate concurrently.
See slides 3–5 for the operating details.

03 / VPS execution & acceptance

A fresh environment for each commit

The VPS persists. Each QA job creates its own Kubernetes cluster and removes it when finished.

01

Freeze & dispatch

Rebase, rerun gates, push the exact SHA. Send the clean QA charter over SSH.

02

Reserve & prepare

Queue for one of two slots. Bootstrap serially: sandbox, private Docker, Kind, normal Tilt and seeded data.

03

Try to break it

Ready slots validate concurrently: tests, APIs, persisted data and authenticated browser behavior.

04

Clean & publish

Clean only owned resources, release the slot and publish evidence. Failed cleanup quarantines capacity.

PASS

The checker validates attempt, commit and evidence integrity. The lead reads the evidence before advancing to PR and CI.

FAIL

Reproduce defects and confirm scope before fixing. Maximum two fix rounds. Bank unrelated findings.

INCOMPLETE

Repair QA and rerun the same commit. After two failed reruns, escalate. An interrupted check cannot pass.

Authentication target: use the stored Clerk credentials for a real session and seed the matching identity. Both parallel trials passed authenticated checks using the same approved account in separate browser sessions. Do not silently replace real authentication with USER_SESSION.

04 / Inside the QA job

What Codex checks on the VPS

The charter defines the required coverage. Every completed check produces evidence for the lead.

Claude lead

Push the frozen SHA. Send acceptance criteria and the QA charter.

→
VPS runner

Reserve a slot. Check out the commit. Bootstrap isolated Kind, Tilt and seeded data.

↓ Codex starts inside the VPS

Lead judges

Check the manifest and evidence. Confirm defects before requesting fixes.

←
Codex Astra

Run the validation ladder. Return verdict.json, logs and evidence.

Two slots validate concurrently; bootstrap is serialized. Each owns its Docker daemon, database, processes, network, temporary files and HOME. Cleanup leaves neighboring attempts running.

  1. Static gates

    Lint and type checks on the exact checkout.

  2. Unit and integration tests

    Affected packages and relevant dependents. Check that tests detect broken behavior.

  3. Real APIs and database

    Verify persisted fields and side effects, beyond the HTTP response.

  4. Authenticated browser flows

    Playwright uses the job’s app and checks the expected Clerk identity.

  5. Adversarial scenarios

    Missing permissions, empty data, invalid inputs and repeated actions.

Acceptance rule: static gates and tests are mandatory. Other checks follow the charter. Missing required coverage means INCOMPLETE. A real-session check cannot silently use USER_SESSION.

05 / Operations & compatibility

Two slots, durable attempts

QA continues after SSH disconnects. Additional attempts wait for capacity.

Reconnect to the same attempt

run-codex-qa --status "$ATTEMPT"
run-codex-qa --collect "$ATTEMPT"
verdict-check.sh "$ATTEMPT" "$PWD" --remote

Use the printed absolute attempt directory. Collection never redispatches. To stop it deliberately: run-codex-qa --cancel "$ATTEMPT".

Recovery and cleanup

systemd supervises each attempt. A reaper recovers interrupted jobs. Failed cleanup quarantines the slot; retained environments hold capacity until release or expiry.

Regular Tilt stays unchanged

No Pantheon changes. Protocol 5 runs original commits inside mandatory sandboxes with private Docker and normal Tilt paths. No staging prerequisite or serial remote fallback.

Scoped isolation proof passed

Two original commits ran in private-Docker sandboxes. Removing A left B’s API, web and Kubernetes healthy; a third job admitted after slot release and cancelled cleanly. B passed all five rungs, the exact-source remote verdict checker, and clean teardown.

Runtime isolation and real supervisor integration pass; two sandbox slots are installed. Six-service scope only. A’s later browser observer had two transient failures (49/51 healthy), then recovered. Broader capacity, retention/reboot and a second VPS remain unverified. Worker selection is explicit; automatic cross-worker balancing is not implemented.
